name: Bayon at Angkor Thom
description: A temple in the Khmer capital of Angkor Thom, constructed in the late 12th or early 13th century CE.

name: Bodhgaya
description: A town in India traditionally identified as the place in which Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment. One of the four main Buddhist pilgrimage sites, it is home to the Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Varaha Cave
description: The modern name of a seventh-century Pallava cave temple in Mahābalipuram.

name: Ganeshwar
description: Chalcolithic settlement in modern Rajasthan, India. The pre-Harappan settlement, located near copper mines and inhabited during the 4th-3rd millennia BCE, is one of two type-sites of the Ganeshwar-Jodhpura Cultural Complex.

name: Dharmaraja Cave
description: Modern name of a seventh-century Pallava cave temple in Mahābalipuram.

name: Mahabodhi Temple
description: One of the four main Buddhist pilgrimage sites, identified as the place where Gautama Buddha attained Enlightenment. The first temple on the site was built by Emperor Asoka in the third century B.C., and the present temple dates from the fifth or sixth centuries. It is one of the earliest Buddhist temples built entirely in brick, still standing in India, from the late Gupta period. The site was largely abandoned from the twelfth-eighteenth centuries. It was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002.

name: Five Rathas
description: The Five Rathas is the modern name of a group of five seventh-century Pallava rock-cut temples at Mahābalipuram.

name: Basawakkulama Tank
description: A reservoir at Anurādhapura in north-central Sri Lanka, originally built in the 4th century BCE and still in use today.

name: Madhukeshwara temple
description: A Shiva temple at Banavasi in India whose foundation may date as early as the 7th century CE.

name: Tanda
description: 16th-century city of Bengal in South Asia

name: Punjeri
description: Modern location in the vicinity of Mamallapuram that may have been the site of a port or harbor facility for the ancient city.

name: Pattadakal
description: A group of temples featuring nine Hindu temples and a Jain sanctuary dating to the seventh and eighth centuries CE and connected with the Chalukya dynasty.

name: Cave 5 at Udayagiri
description: Cave 5 at Udayagiri is dedicated to Vishnu and contains a monumental relief panel of Vishnu's Varaha avatar.

name: Prinas (river)
description: Pliny the Elder describes the ancient Prinas River as a navigable river that debouches into the Ganges. The Barrington Atlas Map-by-Map Directory indicates that the Prinas corresponds to the modern Tons River. The Tons is a modern-day tributary of the Yamuna River (the ancient Iomanes/Iobares), itself the second-largest tributary of the Ganges.

name: Koh Ker
description: An ancient temple complex of the Khmer Empire, Koh Ker is also known as Lingapura or Chok Gargyar. The site is located in the Srayong commune of Preah, Vihear province's Kulen district. The site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in September 2023 and covers some 1,187 ha.

name: Karkabhat
description: Megalithic site in Chhattisgarh, India containing over 800 burials and several stone monuments dated to the first millennium BCE.

name: Srah Srang
description: Large baray or reservoir at Angkor constructed in the 10th century CE.

name: Vaiṣṇava Temple at Udayagiri
description: Temple constructed near the Udayagiri cave complex during the Gupta period (ca. 4th-5th century CE).

name: Rakhigarhi
description: Large settlement and necropolis site in Haranya, India, associated with the Harappan culture (6000-1900 BCE).

name: Mamallapuram
description: An ancient settlement and modern town (also known as Mahabalipuram) located on the east coast of peninsular India. It is the site of a large complex of Hindu temples dating to the 7th/8th centuries CE that is registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city is mentioned in Tamil literature beginning in the 8th century CE. The exact location of the city's harbor and its possible identification with non-Tamil sources (especially Roman ones) remain inconclusive.

name: Achutrajpur
description: Ancient settlement and center of Buddhism near modern Banpur with remains from the 7th-12th centuries. Demolished in modern times.

name: Shore Temple of Mahabalipuram
description: The so-called "Shore Temple" of Mahabalipuram is a granite-built tomb at the "Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram" UNESCO World Heritage Site. It dates to the eighth century CE.

name: Rukhaegarh
description: Settlement site near Nalanda, Bihar District, India, containing remains dated from the Northern Black Polished Ware period through the early Medieval period.

name: Nālandā Mahavihara
description: Buddhist monastery and educational center founded during the Gupta Empire (5th century CE). The site was destroyed around 1200 CE. It was located in ancient and medieval Magadha (modern-day Bihar), eastern India.

name: Bhirrana
description: Bhirrana is an archaeological site located in the Fatehabad district of the north Indian state of Haryana. The site's initial occupation predates the so-called Indus Valley civilization with activity beginning in the 8th-7th millennium BCE.

name: Cave 1 at Udayagiri
description: The southernmost cave at Udayagiri, dedicated to an unidentified god.

name: Alahana Parivena
description: A middle to late eleventh century CE monastic college located outside of Polonnaruwa in Sri Lanka that belonged to King Parakramabahu I.

name: Kanchipuram
description: An ancient city of India, founded in the 4th century BCE and frequently mentioned in literature thereafter, is still a center of religious life and architecture, as well as the textile industry.

name: Marakkanam
description: A modern town in the Villupuram district of Tamil Nadu that was firmly identified in the Barrington Atlas as the location of an emporion named "Sopatma", mentioned in the PME.

name: Preah Khan
description: Temple at Angkor dedicated in 1191 CE under Jayavarman VII. The temple entered a period of decline beginning in the 15th century.

name: Group of monuments at Mahabalipuram (Q3522747)
description: This group of sanctuaries was carved out of rock along the Coromandel coast in the seventh and eighth centuries. The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Angkor Wat
description: The principal temple of Angkor, the capital city of the Khmer empire, Angkor Wat was constructed in the 12th century CE. Angkor was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1992.

name: Kaveripumpattinam/Poombuhar
description: This ancient settlement and seaport was located on the southeastern coast of peninsular India in the vicinity of the modern village of Poompuhar/Poombuhar. Excavations (including a wood-then-brick-built wharf carbon-dated to ca. 250 BCE), as well as epigraphic and literary evidence, demonstrate a thriving seaborne trade and Buddhist religious center through to the 7th century CE. The place was known to the Romans as Chaberis (Ptolemy) and Kamara (PME).

Law 1976 (whence BAtlas) places them at the former fortified settlement of Dantapura, "on the southern bank of the river Vamśadharā, three miles from Chicacole Road Station". Dayalan 2019 passes over Law's suggestion in silence and follows Gerini 1909 in identifying Ptolemy's Paloura with modern Palur.

name: Anurādhapura
description: The ancient capital of Sri Lanka from the fourth century BCE to the 11th century CE. It was recorded under the name Anourogrammon by Ptolemy, who notes its primary political status (Basileion). It has sometimes been argued that a "Palaesimundum" mentioned by Pliny in retelling the story of a Sri Lankan embassy to the emperor Claudius is also to be identified with Anourogrammon. A large number of numismatic finds from many periods have been reported in the vicinity.

description: Complex of 20 cave temples in Madhya Pradesh dedicated to the gods Vishnu and Shiva, constructed from the 3rd-5th centuries CE.

name: Devipattinam
description: A modern village located on the Bay of Bengal in Tamil Nadu, just north of the Rameswaram peninsula. Epigraphic and ceramic evidence indicate that the village's antecedent was a thriving locus of maritime trade from the 13th to the 17th centuries CE.

name: Kayal
description: A medieval port city on the Bay of Bengal that seems to have replaced ancient Korkai as landscape change modified the course of the Tamiraparani river and the coastline at its delta.

name: Visakhapatnam
description: Although the present city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh seems to have been founded in the 11th or 12th century CE, archaeological evidence indicates the natural harbor at Visakhapatnam has served as a center of maritime trade from the 4th or 3rd century BCE onward.

name: Banteay Srei
description: Buddhist temple at Angkor, located approximately 20 km northeast of the main temple complex. Dedicated to Shiva, the temple was constructed during the 10th century CE during the reigns of Rajendravarman II and Jayavarman V.

name: Ajanta Caves
description: The Ajanta Caves are among the earliest Buddhist cave monuments and date from the second and first centuries B.C. During the Gupta period (fifth and sixth centuries A.D.), additional decorated caves were added to the group.

name: Nachchaduwa Tank
description: A major modern reservoir in Sri Lanka, located southeast of Anuradhapura. Its original construction is traditionally dated to the late third or early fourth century CE. BAtlas 5 inset labels its geometry as "Megisba Stagnum", a toponym for a swamp or wetland reported by Pliny during the first century CE.

name: Angkor Thom
description: Walled city established as the capital city of the Khmer Empire during the late 12th century CE by Jayavarman VII. The city was abandoned by 1609.

name: Polonnaruwa
description: An ancient city of the Kingdom of Polonnaruwa dating ca. AD 1070. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
description: The Khajuraho Group of Monuments is designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site located in the modern Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. These temples were built during the Chandella dynasty (ca. 950-1050 CE). The remaining temples belong to two different religions – Hinduism and Jainism

name: Sri Ahobila Narasimha Swamy Temple
description: Main temple in Ahobilam dedicated to the man-lion form of the Hindu god Vishnu built or expanded in the 14th century, sacked by the Mughals in 1578, then restored and expanded at various times up to the present day.

name: Siyapur
description: Settlement in Uttar Pradesh, India containing remains dated from the pre-Painted Grey Ware period (1200 BCE) through the Kushana period (3rd century CE).

name: Cave 13 at Udayagiri
description: Cave 13 at Udayagiri, known as the Nārāyaṇa cave, contains a large relief panel of Vishnu's Nārāyaṇa avatar.

name: Ganesh Ratha
description: Modern name of a seventh-century Pallava rock-cut temple at Mahābalipuram.

name: Mangadu Megalithic Site
description: An archaeological site with Iron Age funerary megaliths located in the vicinity of the modern Moonamkutty-Mangad Road in the northeastern portion of India's Kollam municipality. The site was damaged by cashewnut tree farming and is now not visible due to habitation on the site.

name: Ta Prohm
description: Khmer temple at Angkor constructed in 1186 CE under Jayavarman VII.

name: Qutb Minar
description: The second tallest minar (73 m) in India after Minar-E-Fateh was built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak beginning in AD 1192. The monument is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Vessagiriya
description: Vessagiriya is the site of an ancient Buddhist forest monastery in Sri Lanka. It is considered part of the ruined site of Anuradhapura. The monastery was initially built in the middle of the third century BCE and was expanded in the late fifth century CE. A Roman bronze coin, as well as punch-marked coins and/or ingots, were excavated at Vessagiriya in the first decade of the 20th century.

name: Machilipatnam
description: A modern city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, Machilipatnam served as a major port on the Bay of Bengal, from the 16th through the 19th centuries. Some Roman coins and Mediterranean ceramics have been recovered in the area.
